skill.name: secrets-gitleaks
skill.description: Guides safe Gitleaks secret scanning, configuration, CI integration, false-positive review, compliance mapping, and credential remediation for git repositories.
skill.summary: Build and review Gitleaks controls for repositories, developer workflows, and CI pipelines.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, detector examples, placeholders, and expected CI secret references. Three static findings are confirmed, and semantic review found unredacted CI outputs, broad allowlists, mutable dependencies, and unsafe cleanup guidance. No prompt injection or live credentials were found.

remediation.issue: CI examples retain or print unredacted secret findings.
remediation.suggestion: Add --redact, remove full-report log output, restrict artifact access, and minimize report retention.

remediation.issue: The recommended balanced allowlist excludes broad path and value classes.
remediation.suggestion: Use narrowly scoped rule allowlists, remove blanket documentation and test exclusions, and validate changes with representative true-positive tests.

remediation.issue: The xargs troubleshooting command interpolates repository file names into sh -c.
remediation.suggestion: Parse file and line fields separately, validate line numbers, and pass file names as positional arguments without shell interpolation.

remediation.issue: Workflow actions, hooks, and container images use mutable references.
remediation.suggestion: Pin actions and hooks to reviewed commit hashes and containers to immutable image digests. Document a controlled update process.

remediation.issue: Examples use an unconditional git reset and a predictable temporary path.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the reset or guard it on commit success, and create test files with mktemp plus reliable cleanup.

content.value_statement: Hardcoded credentials can expose systems and fail compliance checks. This skill guides Gitleaks scans, configurations, hooks, CI pipelines, triage, and remediation.
actual_capabilities: Guides current-tree and full-history Gitleaks scans.
Provides strict, balanced, and custom Gitleaks configuration templates.
Provides GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, and pre-commit integration templates.
Explains baselines, incremental scans, allowlists, and false-positive review.
Maps secret detection controls to OWASP, CWE, PCI-DSS, SOC 2, and GDPR.
Documents credential rotation and git history cleanup workflows.
limitations: Gitleaks and git must be installed or supplied by the selected CI environment.
Regex and entropy detection can produce false positives and miss unknown secret formats.
Compliance mappings support evidence preparation but do not establish compliance.
The package documents three helper scripts, but the audited file set does not include them.

use_cases.title: Audit a repository
use_cases.description: Run a redacted full-history scan, classify findings, and prepare a prioritized remediation summary.

use_cases.title: Prevent secret commits
use_cases.description: Configure a pre-commit control and focused allowlists for a development team.

use_cases.title: Add a CI security gate
use_cases.description: Adapt a pipeline template to block new secrets and retain protected evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Run a safe repository scan
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan this repository with Gitleaks. Use redaction, inspect current files and git history, then summarize findings without revealing secret values.

prompt_templates.title: Configure pre-commit protection
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Gitleaks pre-commit setup for this repository. Keep allowlists narrow, explain prerequisites, and provide a safe validation procedure.

prompt_templates.title: Build a CI secret gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt the Gitleaks CI template for this platform. Pin dependencies, redact reports, restrict artifacts, and fail only on verified new findings.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an enterprise rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Gitleaks rollout plan using baselines, custom rules, review ownership, remediation deadlines, protected reporting, and measurable compliance evidence.

output_examples.input: Review this repository for exposed credentials.
output_examples.output: Scan complete: three findings require review. The summary lists affected files, rule names, confidence, and rotation priorities without secret values.

output_examples.input: Reduce false positives without weakening production coverage.
output_examples.output: The proposed allowlist targets two verified fixture paths and one exact placeholder. Documentation and source directories remain scanned.

output_examples.input: Prepare a secure GitHub Actions integration.
output_examples.output: The workflow uses immutable dependencies, full history, redacted output, restricted artifacts, and a blocking pull-request check.

best_practices: Use redaction for terminal output, reports, artifacts, and notifications.
Rotate exposed credentials before removing them from current code or history.
Review every allowlist entry and test that representative real secrets remain detectable.
anti_patterns: Do not publish complete findings files or detected values in CI logs.
Do not exclude entire source, documentation, or test trees without documented review.
Do not treat history cleanup as a substitute for credential rotation.

faq.question: Does this skill install Gitleaks?
faq.answer: No. It provides installation guidance and templates, but Gitleaks and git must be available in the working environment.

faq.question: Can Gitleaks prove that a credential is active?
faq.answer: No. It detects credential-like content. Validate exposure through approved provider processes without transmitting secrets to untrusted services.

faq.question: Should scan reports be stored as CI artifacts?
faq.answer: Only when reports are redacted, access is restricted, retention is minimal, and organizational policy permits storage.

faq.question: When should a finding be allowlisted?
faq.answer: Allowlist only after manual verification, with a narrow scope, a documented reason, an owner, and a review date.

faq.question: Does removing a secret from git history resolve exposure?
faq.answer: No. Rotate or revoke the credential first, then coordinate history cleanup and verify downstream caches, forks, and clones.

faq.question: Does this skill guarantee regulatory compliance?
faq.answer: No. It maps scanning activities to common controls, but compliance depends on scope, implementation, evidence, and independent review.
